new.analysis:
Last week did exactly what a first week back should do: three short, equal sessions, pain 0/10 each time, shin quiet the next morning, and heart rate low and steady. That is the signal to progress, but gently.

The step up this week is small on purpose. Total walk-run time rises from about 45 to 48 minutes, and the longest session grows by 3 minutes. The bigger change is inside the session: your running bouts stretch from about 1 minute to 2 minutes, with a 1-minute walk between. That is the piece that gets you toward 30 minutes continuous by mid-October.

The rule from last week still holds. If the shin aches above 3/10 during a run, or feels worse the next morning, stop and repeat the previous session next time instead of adding to it. Four pain-free weeks in a row is what unlocks faster progress, so we are counting week one as banked and treating this as week two.

Keep the physio calf and hip work on its two days, and keep every run easy with no hills, no strides, and no pushing the pace. The pace you ran last week, around 6:45/km on the run portions, is right where it should be.
